Margit Brinck is a nurse at Odense University Hospital and a serving member of the steering group for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database) [^src1]. Her inclusion in the national database's governance structure reflects the interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral nature of Denmark's clinical quality development programs [^src2].

As a member of the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]], Brinck helps oversee the strategic and operational framework for treating atrial fibrillation in Denmark [^src2]. The steering group's mandate covers a broad spectrum of responsibilities, including the legal anchoring of the database, evaluating data validity and coverage limitations, and promoting concrete clinical practices such as structured patient education [^src1] [^src2]. By representing a major university hospital, Brinck ensures that frontline nursing and patient-centered perspectives are integrated into national cardiovascular health policies and evidence-based quality assurance efforts [^src1] [^src2]. 

Official annual reports from both the 2022–2023 and 2024 periods formally list her as part of the steering group, confirming her ongoing role in shaping the standard of care for a common and potentially serious chronic heart disease [^src1] [^src2].
